sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [2020-, accessed 2026-09-20]. Moam River. New Guinea World: mapping the languages of New Guinea (Santa Fe Institute; hosted at Univ. Zürich). Online comparative-historical phonology of the Ataitan ('Moam River') family: Kaje (Andarum), Tanguat, Igom, Tanggu.
sources.note: Reconstructs Proto-Moam River with 14-15 consonants (*m *n *ŋ *p *t *s *k *mb *nd [*ndz] *ŋg *w *r *j *ɣ) and vowels *i *ʉ *u *a, root template (C)VCVC(VC), no clusters, and gives ~79 correspondence tables with c. 675 Tanguat cells drawn from Z'graggen (1972) (e.g. Tanguat loses initial *m, *r, *j, *ɣ in polysyllables; *w -> [w ɣ g]). Nothing is said about stress, accent, tone or pitch for any language. NOTE (wordlist-only data, not a statement): 31 of the quoted Tanguat forms carry an acute accent, always on i (nín 'excrement', iɣíˑp 'name', míŋ-ʌk 'bow', aŋgaːtʉg-ín 'vine', ndʒíg-oːk 'taro'…

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Tanguat = language 57 / Tg)

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1970. Languages of the Western Madang District. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1271-1303. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C13.1271.
sources.note: Tanguat occurs only in the classification table (p.1278 chart: Ataitan: Tangu 55, Igom 56, Tanguat 57 Tg 570, Andarum 58). 'Notes on the typology of the languages' (pp.1279-80) give for the Ramu Phylum six morphosyntactic traits only (number marking, no concordance classes, one possessive class, dual, tense suffixes, no subject/object incorporation); the phonological/prosodic remarks ('absence of phonemes..', 'None of the languages appears to be tonal') are stated for the Madang and Adelbert Range phyla, not for Ramu. No stress or tone statement applicable to Tanguat.
